metaTitle: Christmas Lighting Installers in Ontario: A Guide
metaDescription: How to choose a holiday lighting company in Ontario, including booking lead times, takedown and storage service, realistic costs and red flags.
intro: Seasonal Christmas lighting is booked on a tight calendar, so scheduling lead time and what happens at takedown matter as much as how the display looks on installation day. Storage service, if offered, varies a lot between companies and is worth confirming before you sign.
whatToLookFor: Clear booking windows for install and, separately, for takedown
Commercial-grade lights and clips rated for outdoor seasonal use
A defined takedown date and whether storage is included or extra
Insurance coverage for work done on rooflines and ladders
Straightforward pricing that isn't dependent on a same-day decision
typicalCostNotes: Holiday lighting costs typically scale with the length of roofline, number of trees or shrubs, and any extras like wreaths or timers, and most companies quote per project once they've seen the home. Booking early in the season generally costs less and secures a better install date than calling in late November, when crews are often fully booked. Ask whether takedown and storage are included in the quoted price or billed as a separate visit.
questionsToAsk: How far in advance do we need to book install and takedown?
Is storage of the lights between seasons included or a separate cost?
What happens if a bulb or section fails partway through the season?
Are your crews insured for roofline and ladder work?
Is the takedown date scheduled now, or arranged closer to the time?
redFlags: Pressure to book on the spot with a limited-time discount
No mention of insurance for roofline or ladder work
Vague or missing takedown date once the season ends
